title: Rosalind and the Horizon
premise: Sable Crane smuggles memories—recorded lives, stolen confessions, dying wishes—past the blockade around Meridian Station, a colony the fleet abandoned and officially erased. When a manifest lists a passenger named Rosalind on a ship that never flew, Sable discovers Rosalind was a child evacuated during the colony's last broadcast, and the memory of what really happened aboard the evacuation fleet has been surgically deleted from every surviving record. Carrying that recovered memory as contraband, Sable must outrun a customs officer who helped bury it and reach the truce talks before the ceasefire expires—delivering the truth that could end the war between the fleet and the outer colonies, or ignite it. In the end she chooses to broadcast it openly rather than trade it for her own pardon, accepting exile but giving both sides the same unignorable truth.
about_author: Oscar Crane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests before turning them into fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and excellent coffee.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs a memory chip past orbital customs hidden in a coffin of frozen seed stock, narrating the dead colony below with the dry wit of someone paid not to care. Introduces her ship, the Vesper, and her rule: never open what you carry. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine customs sweep flags her for a passenger listed on a flight log from eleven years ago—a ship, the Aldrin's Hope, that officially never launched. The name is Rosalind. She realizes someone inserted the ghost deliberately, into her paperwork specifically. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Meridian Below
chapters.summary: Sable descends to the half-abandoned station to trace the manifest's origin through a black-market archivist, Ivo, who deals in deleted records. He warns her the name is bait—and that whoever set it knows her real name, which even she barely remembers. Beat: the hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: Officer Vale
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Customs officer Adaeze Vale, who signed the original cover-up as a junior clerk, recognizes the manifest anomaly and requests jurisdiction over Sable's case. We see her guilt and her ambition braided together: exposing the truth would destroy her; hiding it already has. Beat: complicity wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Knew
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Breaking her own rule, she opens an old shipment and finds a memory chip labeled ROSALIND — DO NOT DELIVER, payment from a client who died before collection. Inside: fragments of a child's evacuation, screaming, an airlock cycling early. Beat: horror breaking through detachment.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Fleet communiqués reveal a ceasefire expiring in nineteen days; the outer colonies are arming. Sable realizes the memory she carries isn't just evidence—it's the casus belli both sides are searching for. Beat: stakes widening from personal to planetary.

chapters.title: Ivo's Price
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ivo agrees to reconstruct the corrupted memory but demands payment in Sable's own earliest memory—the one thing she refuses to sell. Their negotiation exposes why she became a smuggler of other people's pasts: she can't afford her own. Beat: vulnerability traded like currency.

chapters.title: Nineteen Years Gone
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV (recovered memory chapters begin). A nine-year-old girl boards the Aldrin's Hope during the evacuation, clutching her mother's recorded goodbye. The ship launches—but the memory shows it was never meant to reach safety. Beat: innocence walking toward a decision made above its head.

chapters.title: The Airlock Decision
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The memory reveals the fleet ordered the evacuation ships scuttled to blame the colonies and justify the blockade; Rosalind's pod was jettisoned by a junior officer who disobeyed—Vale. The child survived; the record didn't. Beat: betrayal at institutional scale.

chapters.title: Run the Blockade
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vale corners the Vesper at dock; Sable burns her best smuggling route to escape, losing her cargo, her credits, and nearly Ivo. First open violence between them. Beat: the cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Colony Everyone Forgot
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, grounded. Hiding on Meridian's surface, she walks the sealed habitats and finds survivors—unregistered, forgotten, keeping gardens in dead air. For the first time the 'cargo' has faces. Beat: belonging discovered among the discarded.

chapters.title: Vale's Confession
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Ordered to destroy the last physical copy of the Aldrin's Hope logs, Vale instead copies them—and records her own confession into the same chip, a smuggler's format she learned from the case file. Beat: corruption cracking from inside.

chapters.title: Two Chips, One Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable intercepts Vale's confession chip through Ivo's network without knowing its source; Vale realizes her message is loose. Both women now hold halves of the same story and are being hunted by the same fleet tribunal. Beat: enemies converging.

chapters.title: Ivo Betrayed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Fleet agents torture Ivo for her location; he gives up a false route and dies buying her hours. Grief hardens Sable's mission from delivery into testimony. Beat: mourning converted to resolve.

chapters.title: The Tribunal's Offer
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. The tribunal offers Vale full immunity to testify that the colonies scuttled their own ships—the lie she once filed. Accepting means safety and a promotion; refusing means treason. She asks for one day. Beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: Meeting at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Sable and Vale meet face to face in the derelict Aldrin's Hope, still drifting in a decaying orbit. Guns drawn, then lowered; they play Rosalind's memory together in the ship where it happened. Beat: two keepers of the same wound.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The survivors' council offers to trade the memory privately to the colonial armada in exchange for protection—an ending that punishes the fleet but starts the war. Sable must argue against the only people who took her in. Beat: justice versus vengeance.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With hours left on the truce, Sable hijacks the colony's ancient transmitter array and broadcasts the full memory—Rosalind's voice, Vale's confession, the order itself—to both fleets simultaneously, unencrypted, undeniable. Beat: the climax; truth as a weapon aimed at everyone.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Both fleets go quiet mid-attack-run. Vale surrenders herself to the tribunal carrying the original logs, forcing a public inquiry she may not survive. Beat: sacrifice accepted without drama.

chapters.title: Rosalind Found
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following the manifest backward, Sable finds Rosalind alive—adult, renamed, living anonymously on Meridian, having buried the memory herself. Sable offers her the choice no one gave her at nine: speak, or stay silent. Beat: agency returned.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind testifies at the inquiry under her own name, not as evidence but as witness, ending the war's moral pretense on both sides. Vale is convicted of the cover-up but spared execution for her confession. Beat: justice outside the law, finally inside it.

chapters.title: The Horizon
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Pardoned by neither side, Sable keeps the Vesper flying—no longer smuggling memories out, but carrying messages home for the forgotten. Final image: Meridian's lights relighting, seen from orbit, as she turns toward the horizon line. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted.
